title: Local comma criterion for a putative right calculus of fractions
statement:
Use small ordinary categories, nerves, weak homotopy types, quasicategories and right-pinched mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and coherent space-valued functors of [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces], enlarging universes when needed. Let $A$ be a small ordinary category and let $W$ be a subcategory containing all objects and all isomorphisms. Suppose $q:NA\to L$ is a coherent localization: $L$ is a quasicategory, $q$ inverts $W$, and for every quasicategory $E$, restriction identifies $\operatorname{Fun}(L,E)$ with the full subcategory of $\operatorname{Fun}(NA,E)$ on functors inverting $W$. Let $I$ be a small ordinary category with a specified terminal object $i_0$, let $\pi:I\to A$ be a functor, and put $x=\pi(i_0)$. Suppose that $\pi(i\to i_0)$ belongs to $W$ for every $i\in I$. For $y\in A$, define $D_\pi(y)=(\pi\downarrow y)$ to have objects $(i,f:\pi i\to y)$ and arrows $h:i\to i'$ satisfying $f'\pi(h)=f$. An arrow $v:y\to y'$ induces $D_\pi(v)$ by postcomposition. Assume that $ND_\pi(w)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence for every $w\in W$. Then there is a canonical equivalence of weak homotopy types
$$ND_\pi(y)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_L(qx,qy),$$
natural as a comparison of coherent space-valued functors in the entire target variable $y$. The point indexed by $(i,f)$ has component $q(f)q(\pi(i\to i_0))^{-1}$ in $\pi_0\operatorname{Map}_L(qx,qy)$; in particular $(i_0,1_x)$ maps to the identity component. For a second such datum $(A',W',q':NA'\to L',I',i'_0,\pi')$, functors $U:A\to A'$ and $V:I\to I'$ with $U(W)\subseteq W'$, $V(i_0)=i'_0$ and $U\pi=\pi'V$ induce the comma functors $(i,f)\mapsto(Vi,Uf)$ and a localized functor $L\to L'$. The displayed comparisons commute coherently with these functors and with postcomposition in $y$, including coherent diagrams of target maps and composition of maps of these data. Existence of the localization and weak-equivalence invariance of the comma nerves are hypotheses, not conclusions.

proof.text: Work in a universe containing the data and the space infinity-category of [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces]. Define a coherent functor F:NA→𝒮 by F(y)=Sing|ND_π(y)| and by postcomposition on arrows. The objects (i,f) give vertices of F(y). For every h:i→i' the arrow in D_π(π i') from (i,π(h)) to (i',1) gives the edge F(π h)(i,1)→(i',1); chains and degeneracies give a coherent transformation λ:Δ_I*→Fπ.

proof.text: For each $y$, the pullback $NI\times_{NA}(NA)_{/y}$ is canonically $ND_\pi(y)$, including all simplices, and the local cocone induced by $\lambda$ is the singular realization unit $u_{ND_\pi(y)}$. The unit is a weak homotopy equivalence by [lem-cbc-realization-singular-unit-weak]. Unfolding the internal functor simplicial set and coherent transformations in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], an $n$-simplex of $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal S)}(\Delta_K *,\Delta_K Z)$ is exactly a map $K\times\Delta^n\to Z$, so this mapping space is $\operatorname{Fun}(K,Z)$ simplicially. Therefore [lem-cbc-kan-mapping-homotopy-invariance] makes precomposition with the unit an equivalence for every Kan complex $Z$. The cocone mapping-space criterion in [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] then proves that every local cocone is colimiting, including the empty case.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-pointwise-lan-mapping-property] to C=NA, K=NI, F₀=Δ_I*, F and λ. The local colimit calculation gives, for every coherent G:NA→𝒮, a natural equivalence of full transformation spaces Map(F,G)≃Map(Δ_I*,Gπ), sending a transformation to its composite with λ. This retains all target parameters and postcomposition maps.

proof.text: Suppose G inverts W. The arrows s_i=π(i→i₀) give a coherent transformation Gπ→Δ_I G(x), whose components are equivalences; [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] makes it an equivalence of diagrams. The terminal arrows also give a natural contraction of I to i₀, and [lem-coef-nerve-natural-homotopy-equivalence] makes NI→Δ⁰ a weak equivalence. Applying [lem-cbc-kan-mapping-homotopy-invariance] identifies Map(Δ_I*,Gπ) with G(x), by evaluation at i₀.

proof.text: The localization hypothesis descends F to a coherent functor F̄:L→𝒮 and identifies its transformation spaces with those of the W-local functor F. Combining the preceding two steps gives, naturally for every H:L→𝒮, Map(F̄,H)≃H(qx), with evaluation at the point e∈F̄(qx) indexed by (i₀,1_x).

proof.text: Construct the coherent corepresentable $R_{qx}(z)=\operatorname{Map}_L(qx,z)$ from the right-fibration slice of [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration]. The right-pinch comparison and composition classes of [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison] and [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition], together with the covariant construction in [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces], give the full evaluation equivalence for every coherent $H:L\to\mathcal S$: a transformation $\alpha:R_{qx}\to H$ is sent to $\alpha_{qx}(1_{qx})$, and an $n$-simplex $z$ of $H(qx)$ is sent to the parameterized family $f\mapsto H(f)(z)$ on the right-pinched mapping simplices. The composition homotopies make these assignments mutually inverse simplicially, including faces, degeneracies and all parameters. Equivalently, [lem-coef-pointwise-lan-mapping-property] applied to $C=L$, $K=\Delta^0$, $F_0=*$ and this identity cocone records the same full-space equivalence. Thus $\operatorname{Map}(R_{qx},H)\simeq H(qx)$, by evaluation at the identity edge.

proof.text: The two evaluation equivalences show that the transformation c:R_{qx}→F̄ carrying the identity edge to e is an equivalence: take H=R_{qx} to obtain a left inverse, then take H=F̄ and use injectivity of precomposition with c on the full mapping space to obtain the right inverse. Restricting the resulting equivalence along q yields ND_π(y)≃Map_L(qx,qy), coherently in y.

proof.text: Write $s_i=\pi(i\to i_0)$. Naturality of $\lambda$ gives $F(s_i)(i,1)\simeq e$. The comma leg at $(i,f)$ is $F(f)(i,1)$, so under the corepresentable identification its component is $q(f)q(s_i)^{-1}$; at $(i_0,1_x)$ it is the identity. For a map of data $(U,V)$, the induced comma functor and localized functor carry $\lambda$ and $e$ to their primed counterparts. The two resulting coherent transformations are equal after evaluation at the common identity point, hence equal by the full evaluation equivalence of steps 3 and 6. [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] supplies associativity and identity homotopies. For any coherent parameter simplex, the same evaluation equality holds on every face and degeneracy; [lem-cbc-kan-fibration-fiber-criterion] says the homotopy fibers of this evaluation equivalence are contractible, so the pointwise comparisons extend uniquely up to a contractible space of coherent choices. This proves naturality in target maps, data maps and their compositions.
